title: add-fallback-metric-derivations-and-lazy-trace-hydration
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce derived fallback metrics for token cost estimates, opt-in lazy trace hydration to reduce load on the trace store, and debursting smoothing for token-cost alerts. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: In high-cardinality workloads we still see missing token-level counters when upstream aggregators drop or when the path sampler excludes a small fraction of requests. This PR introduces two complementary approaches: 1) fallback/derived metrics that estimate token cost and latency from stable low-cardinality counters and model metadata, and 2) lazy trace hydration which stores lightweight span references in the normal path and only expands full span payloads when an alert or UI action requires it. Together these reduce load on metrics ingestion and tracing backends while preserving observability signal for alerting and on-demand debugging.

What this change does (single continuous description): Adds a derived.metrics pipeline that consumes request-level aggregates (requests.count, tokens.total, runtime.ms.p50/p95) and model variant metadata to synthesize derived.per_token_cost_estimate and derived.per_token_latency_estimate. These metrics are emitted with a "fallback" tag when original per-request token counters are missing. Introduces a lightweight trace envelope (trace.ref) recorded for all requests; the envelope contains parent ids, minimal timing, token-count estimate, and a storage pointer. Full span payloads are routed to an auxiliary object store and only hydrated back into the trace index on-demand (alert escalation, manual inspect, or automated bug-analyzer run). Adds a debursting operator to alert rules: TokenCost:Deburst which smooths short-lived spikes across a taper window and suppresses flapping alerts for noisy workloads.

Commits summary: - 7f3a2c5: add derived metrics pipeline and schema changes - 2b9d1a8: implement fallback tagging and exporter integration - 81c4d2e: introduce trace envelope and storage pointer flow - b4a7f0c: lazy hydration worker + object store integration + retries - ccd9e70: add debursting operator for alert rules and example rule migration - 3a2b7e1: console dashboard tiles + docs and unit tests

Files changed (high level): - telemetry/derived_pipeline.py: new pipeline implementation and unit tests - telemetry/schemas/derived.yaml: metric schema additions - tracing/envelope.go: lightweight trace envelope and pointer plumbing - tracing/hydration/worker.py: background hydrator and retry logic - console/src/components/derivedMetricsTile.tsx: dashboard tile and drilldown links - alerts/rules/token_cost_deburst.rule: new rule + migration script - docs/observability/fallback-derived-metrics.md: design doc and migration notes - infra/helm/templates/hydrator-deployment.yaml: optional worker deployment flags

Testing and CI: Local unit tests for pipeline logic and hydration worker added. Integration test harness runs a synthetic workload with sampling disabled and verifies derived metrics appear with fallback tag and dashboard drill-down hydrates a trace successfully. CI: build/test/lint all passed on latest run; e2e intermittently flaky on CI due to object-store timeouts but we added retries and the run that merged passed after re-run.

Reviewer conversation (condensed as continuous text): Jordan Lee: "Nice approach; can we avoid adding high-cardinality labels to derived metrics?" Maya: "We explicitly limit derived metrics to low-cardinality labels (model, region, route) and add a 'fallback=true' tag; removed user/session ids from emitted metrics." Carlos Mendez: "Hydration path looks good but needs idempotent retries for object-store reads." Maya: "Added backoff+idempotency token and unit tests covering retry scenarios." Priya Rao: "Alert debursting is useful but make sure incidents still escalate if sustained." Maya: "Deburst operator parameterized by window and threshold; rule migration keeps previous behavior by default and requires opt-in to aggressive debursting." Carlos: "Approve after minor docs tweak." Jordan: "Approve" Priya: "Approve (with docs tweak applied)"

Backward compatibility and rollouts: All changes are backwards compatible. Derived metrics are emitted under the derived.* namespace and only used by new dashboards and alert rules. Hydration is opt-in at the infra level (helm toggle) and default behavior records minimal envelopes that are less heavy than full spans. We included a migration script to convert two noisy token-cost alert rules to use TokenCost:Deburst and preserved existing rule behavior under a compat flag.

Operational notes and observability: - New Prometheus/ingest mapping documented; derived metrics default retention reduced to 7d to control cost. - Hydration worker has a concurrency limit, assess via hydration.{active,queued}.metrics. - Added SLO for hydration latency (95th < 10s for on-demand hydrating). - Added dashboard: "Derived Metrics Explorer" and "Hydration Insights" with quick filters for fallback=true.

Risk and mitigation: Primary risk is under/over-estimation from derived metrics causing noisy alerting. Mitigations: (a) tag derived metrics as fallback and keep them out of default SLOs, (b) provide a calibration mode that runs derived side-by-side with original counters for 2 weeks, (c) deburst smoothing to reduce flapping.

Migration steps: 1) Deploy pipeline with calibration mode enabled for 2 weeks. 2) Enable hydrator deployment behind helm flag for on-demand hydration. 3) Migrate alerting rules to TokenCost:Deburst in a staged fashion (canary -> wide). 4) After validation, remove calibration mode and promote derived metrics into dashboards/routed SLOs.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main. Changelog entry added and small follow-up TODOs created: ENG-4032 (add more unit tests for hydrator failure modes), ENG-4033 (add example for customers on how to opt into derived metrics), and ENG-4034 (monitoring playbook updates).
